related_questions.question: What are the new requirements for travel to the UK?

text_blocks.snippet: For US citizens traveling to the UK starting January 8, 2025, an Electronic Travel Authorization (ETA) is required for entry or transit through the UK. This requirement applies to those not needing a visa for short stays, including tourism, business, or family visits. The ETA is digitally linked to your passport and is valid for two years. You can apply online through the UK ETA website or the UK ETA mobile app.
snippet_highlighted_words: an Electronic Travel Authorization (ETA) is required for entry or transit through the UK

list.snippet: Who needs it: US citizens traveling to the UK for visits of up to six months, including transit through UK airports, who do not already have a UK visa.
Validity: Two years or until the passport expires, whichever comes first.
How to apply: Apply online through the UK ETA website or mobile app.
Important Note: Travelers without an approved ETA will be denied boarding.
Passport Validity: Your passport must be valid for the duration of your stay.
Transit through UK Airports: If transiting without passing through border control, an ETA may not be required.

text_blocks.snippet: In essence, if you are a US citizen planning a trip to the UK starting January 8, 2025, you will need to apply for an ETA before traveling. This applies even if you are just passing through a UK airport (transiting).

related_questions.question: What do I need to visit the UK?

text_blocks.snippet: To visit the UK, you'll generally need a valid passport. U.S. citizens, for instance, will need an Electronic Travel Authorization (ETA) for short visits starting January 8, 2025, if they don't have a UK visa or legal residency. Depending on your nationality and purpose of visit, you may also need a standard visitor visa.
1. Valid Passport: You must have a passport valid for the duration of your stay.
2. Electronic Travel Authorization (ETA): If you're a U.S. citizen traveling for tourism, family visits, or short-term business, you'll need an ETA, starting January 8, 2025.
3. Standard Visitor Visa: If you don't qualify for an ETA or if your visit is for longer than 6 months, you might need a Standard Visitor visa.

list.snippet: Proof of funds: Demonstrate you can support yourself during your stay.
Onward ticket: You may need proof of a ticket to leave the UK.
Details of your travel history and purpose: This might be asked for during the application process or at the border.
Contact information for your employer, family, or sponsors: You may need to provide details about who is paying for your trip or if you have family in the UK.
TB test certificate: If you are staying for more than 6 months.

text_blocks.snippet: 5. Common Travel Areas: Special rules apply to those traveling within the Common Travel Area (UK, Ireland, Jersey, Guernsey, and the Isle of Man).
